newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Argentaria unit to cut 2,100 staff.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Argentaria unit to cut 2,100 staff.

text.p: Spain's Banco Exterior de Espana (BEX), a unit of Argentaria, presented late Tuesday a plan to cut staff by 2,100 over three years.
The plan aims to produce "a solution to problems as soon as possible and tranform BEX into a competitive bank in all different business areas," chief executive Federico Outon said in a statement.
The bank added that staff levels, which now total 9,000, needed to be cut urgently, as personnel costs now outstrip ordinary margin.
The efficiency ratio in 1996 was 84 percent, 20 points higher than the sector average, the note added.
In order to carry out the plan BEX will suggest 1,500 early retirements and 200 more redundancies with incentives between 1997 and 1999.
Associated costs will be charged to BEX's shareholders' funds, Argentaria said.
